newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Seventeen killed in combat in northern Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Seventeen killed in combat in northern Colombia.

text.p: At least 15 Marxist-led rebels and two army soldiers have been killed in combat in northwest Colombia, military officials said on Monday.

They said the fighting in the notoriously violent region of Uraba, near the border with Panama, began on Sunday between two counterinsurgency battalions and some 200 Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) guerrillas.

The commander of the Uraba-based 17th Army Brigade confirmed the death toll of 17 in a statement and indicated it could rise, since the battle continued on Monday evening. At least four soldiers have been wounded, the statement said.

The fighting in a rural area of the banana-growing region known as Arenas Altas, outside the Caribbean port of Turbo, erupted while the FARC was staging a high-profile ceremony on Sunday in southern Caqueta province in which it released 70 captive soliders -- 60 of whom had held since the FARC scored a major battlefield victory on Aug. 30 of last year.

The negotiated release of the troops, which came after the government bowed to demands for a temporary demilitarization of a huge jungle-covered area of Caqueta, is widely believed to have enfuriated senior military commanders.
It has, however, led senior government officials, headed by President Ernesto Samper, to voice hopes of jump-starting peace talks with the guerrillas.
The FARC is Colombia's largest and oldest rebel group. It was founded as a pro-Cuban guerrilla force in 1964.
